areas.name: Fear, worry and the heavy mind
areas.line: When the mind will not rest or the heart has gone dark.

areas.name: Grief, illness and death
areas.line: Loss, sickness, and the end of life.

areas.name: Marriage, love and singleness
areas.line: Marriage under strain, dating, and life single.

areas.name: Parents, children and family
areas.line: Raising children, aging parents, and the family you have.

areas.name: Friends, conflict and forgiveness
areas.line: The people who hurt you, and the ones you hurt.

areas.name: Work, money and calling
areas.line: Jobs, bills, ambition, and what your life is for.

areas.name: Sin, habits and temptation
areas.line: What keeps pulling you back, and the way out.

areas.name: Faith, doubt and God
areas.line: Questions about God, and a faith that has gone quiet.

areas.name: Who I am
areas.line: Worth, shame, regret, and starting again.

areas.name: Time, rest and the pace of life
areas.line: Busyness, decisions, change, and keeping going.

areas.name: Church and the world
areas.line: Church life, wounds, politics, and living as a Christian in public.

topics.label: A Wayward Child
topics.line: Few griefs cut like watching a child you raised walk away from the faith, the family, or the life you hoped for them.
phrases: child wants nothing to do with god
topics.framing: Few griefs cut like watching a child you raised walk away from the faith, the family, or the life you hoped for them. Scripture does not hand you a formula to fix it. It hands you a father who runs down the road, and a God who keeps the porch light burning for people who are still in the far country.

topics.label: After a Breakup
topics.line: A breakup is a real loss, and Scripture never tells the wounded to pretend otherwise.
phrases: still in love with my ex
topics.framing: A breakup is a real loss, and Scripture never tells the wounded to pretend otherwise. There is grief here to be felt and not rushed, and a God who is near to the brokenhearted long before you feel near to him.

topics.label: Aging and the Changing Body
topics.line: Scripture does not flatter age and it does not despise it.
phrases: cant do what i used to
topics.framing: Scripture does not flatter age and it does not despise it. It names the body's decline honestly, the strong men stooping and the grinders ceasing, and it crowns the same head with gray as a glory, the proof of a life that kept walking.

topics.label: Alcohol and Drinking
topics.line: Scripture blesses wine as a gift that gladdens the heart and warns in the same breath against the cup that masters a person.
phrases: is it a sin to drink
topics.framing: Scripture blesses wine as a gift that gladdens the heart and warns in the same breath against the cup that masters a person. The line is not between drink and no drink but between the one who holds the cup and the one the cup has begun to hold.

topics.label: Anger and Resentment
topics.line: Scripture does not forbid all anger, but it puts a clock on it and a guard around it.
topics.framing: Scripture does not forbid all anger, but it puts a clock on it and a guard around it. The aim is not a person who never burns but one who rules his own spirit, which it ranks higher than taking a city.

topics.label: Anger at God
topics.line: You are allowed to be angry at God.
topics.framing: You are allowed to be angry at God. Scripture is full of believers who brought their rage straight to him rather than away from him, and the surprising thing is that he does not strike them down for it; he stays in the room. Anger at God is often faith refusing to let go of a God it can no longer understand.

topics.label: Anxiety and Worry
topics.line: Anxiety is not a faith failure.
topics.framing: Anxiety is not a faith failure. Scripture meets the anxious not with a scolding but with an invitation to bring everything, and a promise of a peace that stands guard over the mind.

topics.label: Apologizing Well
topics.line: A real apology names the wrong without softening it, owns it without excusing it, and asks for nothing back.
topics.framing: A real apology names the wrong without softening it, owns it without excusing it, and asks for nothing back. Scripture calls this repentance, and it is not groveling. It is the dignity of a person willing to be seen as he actually is. The half-apology that says sorry you felt that way is not repair. It is a second offense wearing the costume of the first.

topics.label: Assurance of Faith
topics.line: Assurance does not rest on the strength of your feelings but on the finished work of Christ and the faithfulness of the God who keeps you.
topics.framing: Assurance does not rest on the strength of your feelings but on the finished work of Christ and the faithfulness of the God who keeps you. Scripture wants you to know, not merely hope, that you belong to him, and it grounds that knowing outside the wavering of your own heart.

topics.label: Backsliding and Drifting
topics.line: Few people decide to leave God.
topics.framing: Few people decide to leave God. They drift, the way a boat drifts from a dock no one tied it to, until one day the shore is small and strange. Scripture names the drift honestly and calls it not a fall off a cliff but a slow leak, and it treats the return as something God himself promises to do for those who have wandered.

topics.label: Beauty and Appearance
topics.line: We are told the body is a project to be perfected and a product to be displayed.
topics.framing: We are told the body is a project to be perfected and a product to be displayed. Scripture refuses both lies. It says charm is deceptive and beauty fleeting, and that the Lord looks not on the outward appearance but on the heart, where the imperishable beauty actually grows.

topics.label: Being Discipled
topics.line: No one grows up in the faith alone.
topics.framing: No one grows up in the faith alone. Scripture assumes the Christian life is learned the way every deep thing is learned, beside someone further along who lets you watch how it is done. To be discipled is not a program but a relationship, the older walking with the younger until the younger can walk with another.

topics.label: Being Reliable
topics.line: Reliability is faithfulness in the small thing, repeated until it becomes a character.
topics.framing: Reliability is faithfulness in the small thing, repeated until it becomes a character. Scripture promises that the one who is faithful in little is given much, and it does not ask for brilliance, only for a person who does what he said he would do, when he said he would do it. Most trust is not won by a grand act. It is built quietly, by being there, again and again.

topics.label: Betrayal
topics.line: Betrayal is a wound the betrayer chose to give you, and Scripture does not rush past it.
topics.framing: Betrayal is a wound the betrayer chose to give you, and Scripture does not rush past it. It records the friend who turned, the kiss that handed Jesus over, the psalmist undone not by an enemy but by a companion he once walked with to the house of God.

topics.label: Body Image and Worth
topics.line: Your worth was never set by the mirror.
topics.framing: Your worth was never set by the mirror. Scripture says you were knit together with intention and called very good, and it locates your value not in a body that ages but in a God who made it and a Christ who took one on.

topics.label: Breaking Bad Habits
topics.line: A habit is a groove worn into the soul by repetition, and it will not be broken by a single burst of willpower but by a new pattern practiced over time, with grace.
topics.framing: A habit is a groove worn into the soul by repetition, and it will not be broken by a single burst of willpower but by a new pattern practiced over time, with grace. Scripture is honest that the thing you do not want to do is often the thing you keep doing, and it does not leave you there to white-knuckle it alone.

topics.label: Busyness and Overwhelm
topics.line: Busyness is not the same as fruitfulness, and the hurried life is often a way of hiding from the very things that matter most.
topics.framing: Busyness is not the same as fruitfulness, and the hurried life is often a way of hiding from the very things that matter most. Scripture watches Martha distracted with much serving while one thing alone was needful, and it offers the overwhelmed not a better schedule but a different yoke, one that is easy, carried with a Lord who is gentle and lowly.

topics.label: Calling and Purpose
topics.line: Calling is wider than a career and deeper than a job you happen to like.
phrases: what am i supposed to do with my life
topics.framing: Calling is wider than a career and deeper than a job you happen to like. Scripture roots it first in whose you are before what you do, and it dignifies the ordinary work of hands and home as a place where God is served. You do not have to find one perfect role to live a life that matters.

topics.label: Cancel Culture and Shame
topics.line: We have built a machine for public shaming and called it accountability.
topics.framing: We have built a machine for public shaming and called it accountability. It can expose a real wrong, but it offers no road back, no confession that ends in mercy, no door marked grace. Scripture knows the difference between conviction that heals and condemnation that only destroys, and it gives the sinner what the mob never will, a way home.

topics.label: Caring for Aging Parents
topics.line: There comes a day when the parent who carried you cannot carry themselves, and you become the strong one in a relationship that ran the other way your whole life.
topics.framing: There comes a day when the parent who carried you cannot carry themselves, and you become the strong one in a relationship that ran the other way your whole life. Scripture names this reversal not as a burden to be escaped but as a debt of honor to be paid, the commandment to honor father and mother following them into their frailty.

topics.label: Caring for Aging Parents
topics.line: Caring for the parents who once cared for you is heavy, slow, often thankless work, and Scripture counts it as honor rendered to God himself.
topics.framing: Caring for the parents who once cared for you is heavy, slow, often thankless work, and Scripture counts it as honor rendered to God himself. It also knows your strength is finite and never asks you to carry it as though you were alone.

topics.label: Changing Careers
topics.line: To change your work is to ask what your work was ever for.
topics.framing: To change your work is to ask what your work was ever for. Scripture refuses to split the sacred from the so-called secular, treating the daily labor of ordinary hands as something done for the Lord, which means a career change is never only a financial calculation but a question of calling.

topics.label: Cheating and Betrayal of Trust
topics.line: Cheating is the quiet breaking of a promise someone trusted you to keep.
topics.framing: Cheating is the quiet breaking of a promise someone trusted you to keep. Whether in a marriage, a friendship, or a sworn word, it trades a long faithfulness for a short want, and Scripture treats it as a wound to the covenant itself, not merely a private misstep.

topics.label: Chronic Pain and Illness
topics.line: Pain that does not end is its own kind of work, and Scripture does not pretend it away.
topics.framing: Pain that does not end is its own kind of work, and Scripture does not pretend it away. It gives you a God who knows the body from the inside, and a Paul who asked three times for relief and was answered instead with a grace sufficient for the unrelieved.

topics.label: Church Hurt
topics.line: If the church wounded you, your pain is not a sign of weak faith.
topics.framing: If the church wounded you, your pain is not a sign of weak faith. It is the wound that comes from having loved something that was supposed to be safe. Scripture never pretends God's people are clean, and the God who saw your hurt grieves the ones who caused it more than you do.

topics.label: Closeness in Marriage
topics.line: Intimacy is not first a matter of the body but of being fully known and not turned away.
topics.framing: Intimacy is not first a matter of the body but of being fully known and not turned away. Scripture names the goal as one flesh, two whole lives so woven together that distance in one becomes a wound in both, and it is unembarrassed that this nearness is meant to be a delight.

topics.label: Codependency and Losing Yourself
topics.line: There is a love that gives itself away and a love that disappears itself, and the two are not the same.
topics.framing: There is a love that gives itself away and a love that disappears itself, and the two are not the same. Scripture calls you to lay down your life, but never to lose the self God made and called good; the command to love your neighbor as yourself assumes there is a self there to love.

topics.label: Comparison and Envy Online
topics.line: Comparison is the thief that arrives the moment you measure your ordinary life against someone else's edited one.
topics.framing: Comparison is the thief that arrives the moment you measure your ordinary life against someone else's edited one. Scripture calls envy rottenness in the bones and offers instead a strange contentment, the kind that has learned to be at peace whether the account is full or empty.

topics.label: Complaining and Grumbling
topics.line: Complaining feels like honesty, but Scripture treats the grumbling heart as a serious thing.
topics.framing: Complaining feels like honesty, but Scripture treats the grumbling heart as a serious thing. There is a vast difference between lament, which brings real pain to God, and grumbling, which nurses a grievance against him. One draws near in trust. The other accuses in the dark, and slowly poisons the one who keeps it.

topics.label: Conflict at Work
topics.line: The workplace is where most of us spend our days under people we did not choose, and Scripture has more to say about it than we expect.
topics.framing: The workplace is where most of us spend our days under people we did not choose, and Scripture has more to say about it than we expect. It treats your work as worship and your conduct toward a hard boss or a scheming colleague as a real test of the faith you carry past the church door.

topics.label: Conflict With Others
topics.line: Conflict is not a sign that something has gone wrong with you.
topics.framing: Conflict is not a sign that something has gone wrong with you. Scripture assumes it will come even among people who love each other, and it refuses both the avoidance that buries the wound and the explosion that widens it.

topics.label: Consumerism and Stuff
topics.line: The ad does not sell you a thing.
topics.framing: The ad does not sell you a thing. It sells you a self you do not yet have, and tells you the gap can be closed with a purchase. Scripture answers not with a tighter budget but with a deeper word, that a life does not consist in the abundance of possessions.

topics.label: Contentment
topics.line: Contentment is not the absence of wanting but a peace that does not depend on getting.
topics.framing: Contentment is not the absence of wanting but a peace that does not depend on getting. Paul calls it something he had to learn, a secret available in plenty and in want alike, grounded not in his circumstances but in the One who holds them.

topics.label: Courage and Fear
topics.line: Courage in Scripture is not the absence of fear but the presence of something stronger than fear.
topics.framing: Courage in Scripture is not the absence of fear but the presence of something stronger than fear. It is rooted not in the size of your nerve but in the promise that God goes with you, and so its command is almost always paired with a reason, be strong and courageous, for the Lord your God is with you.

topics.label: Crude and Cutting Talk
topics.line: Scripture takes the tongue more seriously than we do, calling it a small thing that sets a whole life on fire.
topics.framing: Scripture takes the tongue more seriously than we do, calling it a small thing that sets a whole life on fire. The question is not only what slips out when you are angry but what your everyday speech is quietly doing to the people who have to hear it.

topics.label: Dating a Nonbeliever
topics.line: This is one of the tender ones, because the heart has usually moved before the question gets asked.
phrases: date someone who isnt a christian
marry someone who isnt a christian
break up because hes not saved
topics.framing: This is one of the tender ones, because the heart has usually moved before the question gets asked. Scripture does not despise the person who does not share your faith, but it is honest that two people walking toward different homes will feel the strain at the deepest place, where it matters most.

topics.label: Dating and Discernment
topics.line: Dating is not in the Bible, but discernment is, and so is the kind of love Scripture means to build toward.
phrases: how do i know if hes the one
how do i know if shes the one
should we get married or wait
is he the right person to marry
is she the right person to marry
topics.framing: Dating is not in the Bible, but discernment is, and so is the kind of love Scripture means to build toward. The question is less whether the feeling is strong than whether the person beside you is honest, kind, and walking the same direction you are.

topics.label: Decision Fatigue and Overwhelm
topics.line: An endless menu of choices is not freedom but a kind of exhaustion, and a heart that must decide everything from scratch wears thin by noon.
topics.framing: An endless menu of choices is not freedom but a kind of exhaustion, and a heart that must decide everything from scratch wears thin by noon. Scripture does not hand you a flowchart for every fork in the road. It offers something better, the promise that the one who asks for wisdom will be given it, without reproach.

topics.label: Decisions and Guidance
topics.line: God's guidance is more often a settled character than a secret map.
topics.framing: God's guidance is more often a settled character than a secret map. Scripture promises wisdom to those who ask and a light for the next step, not a blueprint of the whole road. The aim is not to crack a code but to become the kind of person who chooses well.

topics.label: Deep Friendship
topics.line: Real friendship is one of the great gifts and great losses of a life, and Scripture takes it seriously enough to honor it as a love in its own right.
topics.framing: Real friendship is one of the great gifts and great losses of a life, and Scripture takes it seriously enough to honor it as a love in its own right. It praises the friend who sticks closer than a brother and warns that the wrong company will quietly reshape who you become.

topics.label: Defensiveness
topics.line: Defensiveness is the reflex to protect a self that does not feel safe enough to be wrong.
topics.framing: Defensiveness is the reflex to protect a self that does not feel safe enough to be wrong. The moment a word of correction lands, the lawyer in us stands up, and we spend on excuses and counter-charges the strength that could have gone to listening. Scripture calls the willingness to be corrected a mark of wisdom, and the refusal of it a mark of the fool.

topics.label: Depression and Despair
topics.line: Depression is not a sin and it is not a lack of faith.
topics.framing: Depression is not a sin and it is not a lack of faith. Scripture gives the despairing their own voice in the darkest of the Psalms, and shows us prophets and apostles who wanted to die and were not scolded but fed, rested, and kept.

topics.label: Difficult Family
topics.line: The Bible is not a book of tidy families.
phrases: never good enough for my parents
topics.framing: The Bible is not a book of tidy families. Its pages are full of jealous brothers, scheming parents, and households that wound, and it tells the truth about them rather than smoothing it over, while still calling us to honor where we can and guard where we must.

topics.label: Disappointment
topics.line: Disappointment is the ache of the gap between what you hoped for and what came.
topics.framing: Disappointment is the ache of the gap between what you hoped for and what came. Scripture does not minimize it, naming hope deferred as a sickness of the heart, and yet it refuses to let the disappointed conclude that God has failed them.

topics.label: Division in the Church
topics.line: Division is the oldest disease in the church, and it almost never arrives wearing the name of pride.
topics.framing: Division is the oldest disease in the church, and it almost never arrives wearing the name of pride. It comes dressed as principle, as discernment, as standing for truth. Scripture takes it with deadly seriousness, because the watching world reads the gospel mostly in how we treat each other.

topics.label: Doubt and Questions
topics.line: Doubt is not the opposite of faith.
topics.framing: Doubt is not the opposite of faith. It is often faith under pressure, honestly facing its questions, and Scripture is full of believers who brought their doubts straight to God rather than away from him.

topics.label: Encouraging Others
topics.line: Encouragement is not flattery but the steady gift of telling someone the truth that holds them up.
topics.framing: Encouragement is not flattery but the steady gift of telling someone the truth that holds them up. Scripture treats it as a real ministry, a thing the body of Christ owes one another daily, because the discouraged heart cannot always carry itself and was never meant to.

topics.label: Envy and Comparison
topics.line: Envy is grief at another person's good, and it eats the one who carries it.
topics.framing: Envy is grief at another person's good, and it eats the one who carries it. Scripture calls it rottenness in the bones and the thing that handed Jesus over to die, and it answers comparison not by winning the contest but by leaving it.

topics.label: Estrangement and the Cut-Off
topics.line: An empty chair at the table is its own kind of grief, the loss of someone who is still alive.
phrases: wont let me see my grandchildren
topics.framing: An empty chair at the table is its own kind of grief, the loss of someone who is still alive. Scripture does not pretend these breaks are simple, but it keeps the door open longer than we would, and it tells the story of a father who watched the road every day.

topics.label: Exhaustion and Burnout
topics.line: Exhaustion is not a badge and it is not a sin, but it is a signal.
topics.framing: Exhaustion is not a badge and it is not a sin, but it is a signal. Scripture gives the tired body something our age refuses it, a built-in stop, a rhythm of rest that says the world will keep turning without your hands on it.

topics.label: Facing a Big Decision
topics.line: Some choices set the course of years, and the weight of them can freeze a person at the fork.
topics.framing: Some choices set the course of years, and the weight of them can freeze a person at the fork. Scripture does not promise a voice from the sky for every turn, but it does promise wisdom to those who ask for it, and it puts the surrender before the certainty, telling you to trust the Lord more than your own grasp of the road ahead.

topics.label: Facing a Terminal Diagnosis
topics.line: To be told your time is short is to have the thing we all push away brought suddenly near, and the fear, the grief, and the disbelief that follow are not a failure of faith but the honest weight of a human being facing the end.
topics.framing: To be told your time is short is to have the thing we all push away brought suddenly near, and the fear, the grief, and the disbelief that follow are not a failure of faith but the honest weight of a human being facing the end. Scripture does not pretend death is small, but it stands at the grave and calls death the last enemy, already defeated by a Savior who walked through it ahead of you.

topics.label: Fear of Missing Out
topics.line: The fear of missing out is the old sin of envy fitted with a screen.
topics.framing: The fear of missing out is the old sin of envy fitted with a screen. It assumes the good life is always somewhere you are not, in a room you were not invited to, and it cannot rest in the one life you were actually given. Scripture answers with a harder and kinder word, that godliness with contentment is great gain.

topics.label: Fear of the Future
topics.line: Some of what we dread is real, and Scripture does not arm us against tomorrow by showing it to us in advance.
topics.framing: Some of what we dread is real, and Scripture does not arm us against tomorrow by showing it to us in advance. It does something better, putting the unknown future in known hands, and telling us the same God who held yesterday already stands in the day we fear.

topics.label: Feeling Far From God
topics.line: Feeling far from God is not the same as being far from him.
topics.framing: Feeling far from God is not the same as being far from him. Scripture is full of saints who felt forsaken at the very moment they were being held, and it teaches you to keep walking by what is true when the feeling has gone quiet.

topics.label: Feeling Stuck
topics.line: Feeling stuck is not the same as being abandoned.
topics.framing: Feeling stuck is not the same as being abandoned. Scripture is full of long stretches where nothing seemed to move, and it teaches that God works as much in the waiting as in the breakthrough, growing the kind of person who can be trusted with what comes next.

topics.label: Financial Hardship
topics.line: Scripture does not pretend that want is easy, and it never blames the poor for their poverty.
topics.framing: Scripture does not pretend that want is easy, and it never blames the poor for their poverty. It meets the one who cannot pay the bills with a God who feeds birds and clothes fields, and asks whether you are worth less to him than they are.

topics.label: Finding a Church
topics.line: Finding a church is not finding a perfect church, because none exists and you would not fit it if it did.
topics.framing: Finding a church is not finding a perfect church, because none exists and you would not fit it if it did. Scripture calls you not to a building or a brand but to a body, a particular set of people you will learn to love because they are difficult, and who will love you the same way.

topics.label: Finishing What You Start
topics.line: Beginnings are cheap.
topics.framing: Beginnings are cheap. The crowd is always large at the start and thin at the finish, and Scripture reserves its honor for the one who endures to the end, who counts the cost before he builds and then builds it through. To leave a thing half-done is not only to waste the work already spent. It is to train yourself in the habit of leaving.

topics.label: Food and Eating
topics.line: Food in Scripture is never merely fuel.
topics.framing: Food in Scripture is never merely fuel. It is gift, fellowship, and a daily reminder that you do not feed yourself from nothing, and the table is one of the chief places where grace becomes visible and shared.

topics.label: Gambling and the Bet
topics.line: Scripture never names the lottery, but it names the heart that wants wealth without work and money it has not earned.
topics.framing: Scripture never names the lottery, but it names the heart that wants wealth without work and money it has not earned. The bet promises that one night can undo a hard life, and that promise is the lie that empties the table.

topics.label: Generosity and Giving
topics.line: Generosity is not mainly a transfer of money but a loosening of the grip, the proof that you trust the Giver more than the gift.
topics.framing: Generosity is not mainly a transfer of money but a loosening of the grip, the proof that you trust the Giver more than the gift. Scripture ties it to joy, calling God the lover of a cheerful giver, and treats the open hand as the surest cure for the quiet greed that hardens a heart.

topics.label: Generosity with Time
topics.line: We guard our time more fiercely than our money, and call it stewardship when it is often hoarding.
topics.framing: We guard our time more fiercely than our money, and call it stewardship when it is often hoarding. Scripture shows a Jesus repeatedly interrupted, by the bleeding woman, by the children, by the blind man on the road, and he treats the interruption not as a theft from his agenda but as the actual work. The most generous thing many of us could give is not a check. It is an unhurried hour.

topics.label: Gentleness and Meekness
topics.line: Gentleness is not weakness, and meekness is not timidity.
topics.framing: Gentleness is not weakness, and meekness is not timidity. Scripture means by them a strength held under control, power that chooses restraint, and it puts the gentle answer forward as the thing that turns away wrath where a harsh word only feeds it.

topics.label: Giving to the Church
topics.line: Giving is not the church collecting a fee from you.
topics.framing: Giving is not the church collecting a fee from you. It is the slow loosening of money's grip on your heart, a discipline Scripture treats as worship and warns against treating as obligation. The question is never only how much the church needs. It is what your wallet reveals about where your trust actually rests.

topics.label: God's Sovereignty
topics.line: Scripture insists that God reigns over all things, and that this is comfort rather than fatalism.
topics.framing: Scripture insists that God reigns over all things, and that this is comfort rather than fatalism. He is not a distant clockmaker nor a tyrant pulling strings, but a Father who works all things, even the ones meant for evil, toward good for those who love him.

topics.label: Gossip and the Tongue
topics.line: Scripture gives more weight to the tongue than we ever do, calling it a fire and a world of harm set among the members of the body.
topics.framing: Scripture gives more weight to the tongue than we ever do, calling it a fire and a world of harm set among the members of the body. Gossip is rarely felt as cruelty by the one doing it, which is exactly why it does so much of its damage unnoticed.

topics.label: Grace and Works
topics.line: Grace and works have been pitted against each other for so long that many people no longer know how they fit.
topics.framing: Grace and works have been pitted against each other for so long that many people no longer know how they fit. Scripture holds both without flinching: we are saved by grace through faith and not by works, and the faith that saves is never alone but always proves itself in a changed life. The tree is not made alive by its fruit, yet a living tree always bears it.

topics.label: Gratitude and Thankfulness
topics.line: Gratitude is not a mood that arrives on good days.
topics.framing: Gratitude is not a mood that arrives on good days. Scripture treats it as a discipline, a deliberate turning toward what you have been given, commanded even in hard seasons because it reorders the heart that is prone to forget.

topics.label: Greed and the Grasping Hand
topics.line: Greed is the hunger that never says enough.
topics.framing: Greed is the hunger that never says enough. Scripture names it not as a sin of the poor or the rich alone but of the human heart, which keeps mistaking the next acquisition for the rest it is actually looking for. Jesus calls us to guard against all of it, because a life does not consist in the abundance of possessions.

topics.label: Grief and Loss
topics.line: Scripture never tells the grieving to pretend.
topics.framing: Scripture never tells the grieving to pretend. It gives them a third of the Psalms as lament, walks them to a graveside where Jesus himself wept, and promises not the absence of the valley but a presence in it.

topics.label: Guilt and Conscience
topics.line: Scripture takes guilt seriously enough to name it real and not merely a feeling to be managed away.
topics.framing: Scripture takes guilt seriously enough to name it real and not merely a feeling to be managed away. But it draws a hard line between the guilt that drives you to God and the guilt that only drives you into the ground, and it answers true guilt not with denial but with a cross.

topics.label: Hardness of Heart
topics.line: Hardness of heart is not a sudden state but the slow result of a thousand small refusals.
topics.framing: Hardness of heart is not a sudden state but the slow result of a thousand small refusals. Each time conscience is overruled, the heart grows a little less able to feel. Scripture warns of it as the most dangerous condition of all, because the hardened heart no longer knows it is hard, and feels its own numbness as peace.

topics.label: Hearing From God
topics.line: God has already spoken, fully and clearly, in his word, and that is where you go first to hear him.
topics.framing: God has already spoken, fully and clearly, in his word, and that is where you go first to hear him. Scripture promises that his sheep know his voice, but it also warns that the heart is easy to deceive, so what you think you hear is always tested against what he has already said.

topics.label: Heaven and Eternity
topics.line: Heaven in Scripture is less a misty escape from earth than the healing of it.
phrases: where do we go when we die
will we know each other in heaven
topics.framing: Heaven in Scripture is less a misty escape from earth than the healing of it. The Christian hope is not disembodied souls on clouds but a new heaven and a new earth, bodies raised, the world remade, and God himself dwelling among his people.

topics.label: Hell and Judgment
topics.line: Hell is the hardest doctrine the church holds, and it should never be held lightly or with relish.
topics.framing: Hell is the hardest doctrine the church holds, and it should never be held lightly or with relish. Scripture presents it not as God's eagerness to punish but as the terrible ratification of a person's refusal of him, the door, as one writer put it, locked from the inside.

topics.label: Honesty and Integrity
topics.line: Integrity is what you are when no one is watching, the whole self matching from the inside out.
topics.framing: Integrity is what you are when no one is watching, the whole self matching from the inside out. Scripture prizes the person whose yes is yes, who keeps his word even when it costs him, and it says such a one walks securely while the crooked path is eventually found out.

topics.label: Hospitality When You Are Tired
topics.line: Hospitality is not entertaining, and the difference is everything.
topics.framing: Hospitality is not entertaining, and the difference is everything. Entertaining waits until the house and the host are impressive. Hospitality opens a real and ordinary table to a real and tired host, because the welcome is the gift, not the performance. Scripture commands it without the condition that you feel up to it, and some of the deepest welcomes are given by those with the least left to give.

topics.label: Hurry and Rush
topics.line: Hurry is not a schedule problem.
topics.framing: Hurry is not a schedule problem. It is a condition of the soul, the steady refusal to live inside the limits God gave a creature, and it quietly erodes the very things that cannot be rushed, prayer, attention, love. Scripture does not praise the busy. It praises the still.

topics.label: Hypocrisy and the Mask
topics.line: Hypocrisy is the gap between the face we show and the life we live.
topics.framing: Hypocrisy is the gap between the face we show and the life we live. The word itself comes from the stage, where an actor spoke behind a mask. Scripture reserves some of its hardest words for it, not because the hypocrite is the worst sinner but because the mask makes repentance impossible, hiding the very wound that needs healing.

topics.label: Identity and Worth
topics.line: The world tells you to build a self out of your achievements, your image, or your performance, and then defend it forever.
topics.framing: The world tells you to build a self out of your achievements, your image, or your performance, and then defend it forever. Scripture says your worth was settled before you produced anything, given by the One who made you in his image and bought you at a price.

topics.label: Idolatry of the Heart
topics.line: An idol is not only a statue.
topics.framing: An idol is not only a statue. It is anything that takes the place meant for God, a good thing made into an ultimate thing, the love that runs your life from underneath. Scripture's first command is also its deepest diagnosis, that the human heart is restless to crown something, and will crown the wrong thing every time it is left to itself.

topics.label: Immaturity
topics.line: Maturity is not about age.
topics.framing: Maturity is not about age. It is the slow work of becoming a person whose wants no longer rule him, who can keep a promise, carry a weight, and put another before himself. Scripture treats this growth as the ordinary expectation of the Christian life and grieves when grown believers are still being fed milk because they cannot stomach solid food.

topics.label: Indecision
topics.line: Indecision often dresses itself as caution, but underneath it is usually fear, the fear of the wrong choice, the fear of regret, the fear of being responsible for a road that goes badly.
topics.framing: Indecision often dresses itself as caution, but underneath it is usually fear, the fear of the wrong choice, the fear of regret, the fear of being responsible for a road that goes badly. Scripture calls the man who cannot settle double-minded and unstable in all his ways, and it offers the paralyzed not a hidden answer to decode but a wisdom freely given to those who ask.

topics.label: Infertility and Childlessness
topics.line: This is a grief the world rarely lets you name out loud, a loss with no funeral and a hope that aches every month.
topics.framing: This is a grief the world rarely lets you name out loud, a loss with no funeral and a hope that aches every month. Scripture does not look away from it. It fills its pages with women who wanted children and waited, and it never once treats their longing as small.

topics.label: Information Overload
topics.line: We were promised that more information would make us wise.
topics.framing: We were promised that more information would make us wise. It has mostly made us anxious. Scripture never equates knowing more with knowing well, and it warns that the heart, not the feed, is what must be guarded, since from it flow the springs of life.

topics.label: Insecurity and Low Self-Worth
topics.line: Insecurity is the nagging sense that you are not enough, measured against everyone you have ever envied.
topics.framing: Insecurity is the nagging sense that you are not enough, measured against everyone you have ever envied. Scripture answers it not by inflating your opinion of yourself but by relocating the question entirely, telling you that your worth was never yours to earn or lose because it was fixed by the One who made you and bought you.

topics.label: Jealousy and Envy
topics.line: Envy is the grief we feel at another's good, and Scripture treats it not as a quirk but as rot in the bones.
topics.framing: Envy is the grief we feel at another's good, and Scripture treats it not as a quirk but as rot in the bones. The cure is not to win the comparison but to be set free from the scoreboard altogether.

topics.label: Job Loss
topics.line: Losing a job takes more than a paycheck.
topics.framing: Losing a job takes more than a paycheck. It can take the role you wore, the worth you measured by it, and the place you held in the world, and Scripture knows the difference between what you do and who you are.

topics.label: Joy and Gladness
topics.line: Joy in Scripture is not the same as a good mood, and it does not depend on good circumstances.
topics.framing: Joy in Scripture is not the same as a good mood, and it does not depend on good circumstances. It is a settled gladness rooted in God himself, the kind Paul could command from a prison cell, deeper than happiness and able to coexist with sorrow.

topics.label: Justice and the Poor
topics.line: God's concern for the poor and the wronged is not a wing of the Bible.
topics.framing: God's concern for the poor and the wronged is not a wing of the Bible. It runs through the whole of it, in the law, the prophets, the wisdom, and the words of Jesus. This is not a borrowed political cause. It is older than every modern party, and it judges all of them.

topics.label: Keeping a Confidence
topics.line: When someone tells you a hard thing, they hand you a piece of themselves to hold.
topics.framing: When someone tells you a hard thing, they hand you a piece of themselves to hold. Scripture is plain that a faithful person covers it, while the gossip spreads it for the small thrill of being the one who knows. The tongue that cannot keep a secret is not merely indiscreet. It has broken trust, and the wreckage often cannot be rebuilt.

topics.label: Keeping Your Word
topics.line: A promise is a small covenant, and covenant is how God has dealt with us from the beginning.
topics.framing: A promise is a small covenant, and covenant is how God has dealt with us from the beginning. Scripture honors the one who swears to his own hurt and does not change, who keeps faith when keeping it costs him. The question is never whether breaking the promise would be easier. It is whether you are a person whose word can be stood on.

topics.label: Kindness and Compassion
topics.line: Kindness in Scripture is not mere niceness, a smoothing over of things.
topics.framing: Kindness in Scripture is not mere niceness, a smoothing over of things. It is a strength that bends toward the weak, the active goodness of God himself, and Scripture says it is his kindness, not his thunder, that leads a hard heart to turn.

topics.label: Knowing God's Will
topics.line: Most of God's will is already revealed and rarely the thing we ask about.
topics.framing: Most of God's will is already revealed and rarely the thing we ask about. Scripture spends far more breath telling you the kind of person to become than the next move to make, and it promises wisdom to anyone who asks for it without hedging.

topics.label: Knowing the Bible
topics.line: Scripture presents itself not as a rulebook to consult but as living words meant to be lived in, read slowly and obeyed, more dwelling than reference.
topics.framing: Scripture presents itself not as a rulebook to consult but as living words meant to be lived in, read slowly and obeyed, more dwelling than reference. To know the Bible is finally to know its author, and the aim of all reading is a changed life, not merely an informed mind.

topics.label: Learning to Trust God
topics.line: Trust is not pretending you are not afraid.
topics.framing: Trust is not pretending you are not afraid. It is choosing to lean your weight on God's character when his ways are hidden, and Scripture grounds that lean not in good outcomes but in who he has shown himself to be.

topics.label: Leaving for College
topics.line: You are leaving the house you were formed in to become someone in a place no one knows you.
topics.framing: You are leaving the house you were formed in to become someone in a place no one knows you. Scripture honors the young who carry their faith into new and testing ground, and it tells them the one thing the campus will try to talk them out of, that the fear of the Lord, not the cleverness of the lecture hall, is where wisdom actually begins.

topics.label: Legalism and Rule-Keeping
topics.line: Legalism is the quiet conviction that God's love is a wage to be earned and a debt that can be paid.
topics.framing: Legalism is the quiet conviction that God's love is a wage to be earned and a debt that can be paid. It dresses up as devotion, and it is in fact a kind of unbelief, a refusal to trust that grace really is free. Scripture treats it not as harmless zeal but as a different gospel that cannot save.

topics.label: Life Transitions
topics.line: There is a kind of suffering that comes not from loss but from change, the ground shifting under a settled life.
topics.framing: There is a kind of suffering that comes not from loss but from change, the ground shifting under a settled life. Scripture knows the unsteadiness of the threshold, and it ties the comfort of the believer not to fixed circumstances but to a God who does not change.

topics.label: Loneliness
topics.line: You were not made to be alone.
topics.framing: You were not made to be alone. Scripture knows you become the average of the people you keep close, and it honors the faithful friend over the flatterer and says a brother is born for the hard day.

topics.label: Longing for Marriage
topics.line: The desire for a spouse is good and God-given, and the ache of it unmet is not a sign of failure or low faith.
phrases: everyone is getting married but me
will god give me a spouse
will i ever find a husband
will i ever find a wife
nobody has ever asked me out
topics.framing: The desire for a spouse is good and God-given, and the ache of it unmet is not a sign of failure or low faith. Scripture neither dismisses the longing nor makes marriage the measure of a life, holding both your wish and your wholeness at once.

topics.label: Losing a Child
topics.line: There is no grief like the death of a child, the loss that breaks the order of things and leaves a parent burying the one they were meant to raise.
topics.framing: There is no grief like the death of a child, the loss that breaks the order of things and leaves a parent burying the one they were meant to raise. Scripture does not flinch from this sorrow, recording the wail of David and the inconsolable weeping of Rachel, and it makes no attempt to explain it away, only to hold the grieving inside a love that does not let go.

topics.label: Losing a Parent
topics.line: When a parent dies, you lose more than a person, you lose the one who knew you first and longest, and a generation steps aside leaving you suddenly at the front of the line.
topics.framing: When a parent dies, you lose more than a person, you lose the one who knew you first and longest, and a generation steps aside leaving you suddenly at the front of the line. Scripture honors this bond all the way to the cross, where Jesus, dying, made sure his mother would be cared for, and it gives full room to mourn the one who gave you life.

topics.label: Losing a Spouse
topics.line: To lose a spouse is to lose the one you became one flesh with, and the tearing is felt in the body, the bed, the empty chair, the thousand small habits built around a person no longer there.
topics.framing: To lose a spouse is to lose the one you became one flesh with, and the tearing is felt in the body, the bed, the empty chair, the thousand small habits built around a person no longer there. Scripture gives the widow and widower a particular tenderness, naming them again and again as those God himself draws near to defend and provide for.

topics.label: Loving Your Enemies
topics.line: The command to love your enemies is the hardest thing Jesus ever said, and he meant it without an exit clause.
topics.framing: The command to love your enemies is the hardest thing Jesus ever said, and he meant it without an exit clause. It does not require warm feeling but active goodwill, the refusal to repay evil with evil even when the evil is real and the enemy unrepentant.

topics.label: Low Motivation
topics.line: Low motivation is rarely just laziness, and it is rarely just one thing.
topics.framing: Low motivation is rarely just laziness, and it is rarely just one thing. Sometimes it is the body asking for rest it has been denied, sometimes it is fear of failing dressed as not caring, and sometimes it is the soul gone dry. Scripture honors honest work and warns against the slow ruin of the sluggard, but it never reduces a weary person to a moral failure.

topics.label: Lukewarm Faith
topics.line: Lukewarm faith is the most respectable failure in the church, because it looks like nothing is wrong.
topics.framing: Lukewarm faith is the most respectable failure in the church, because it looks like nothing is wrong. The fire has not gone out; it has banked to a comfortable warmth that asks little and costs less. Scripture reserves some of its hardest words for it, not because the lukewarm are the worst people but because they no longer feel their need.

topics.label: Lust and the Wandering Eye
topics.line: Lust is not the same as desire, which is a gift.
topics.framing: Lust is not the same as desire, which is a gift. It is desire detached from the person, turning someone made in God's image into a thing to be used. Scripture takes it seriously precisely because it begins in the unseen room of the heart, long before anything is done with the body.

topics.label: Lying and Honesty
topics.line: A lie is rarely told to harm.
topics.framing: A lie is rarely told to harm. It is told to be safe, to be liked, to avoid the cost of the truth, and that is exactly why it is so hard to stop. Scripture treats truthfulness not as a rule but as the very ground people stand on with one another.

topics.label: Marriage After an Affair
topics.line: An affair breaks something that cannot simply be glued back; what is built after is a new thing, made slowly, out of repentance and a thousand small proofs.
topics.framing: An affair breaks something that cannot simply be glued back; what is built after is a new thing, made slowly, out of repentance and a thousand small proofs. Scripture takes the wound seriously, and it also dares to speak of a love that takes back the unfaithful. If the betrayal came with abuse or control, safety comes first; the National Domestic Violence Hotline is 800-799-7233.

topics.label: Marriage Trouble
topics.line: Most marriages do not end in a blowup but in a slow drift no one decided on.
topics.framing: Most marriages do not end in a blowup but in a slow drift no one decided on. Scripture frames marriage as covenant, not contract, and gives it the one tool without which no marriage survives, forgiveness offered as freely as you have received it.

topics.label: Mending What Broke
topics.line: Reconciliation is not forgetting the wrong but doing the harder thing, facing it together and refusing to let it have the last word.
phrases: say im sorry after all these years
topics.framing: Reconciliation is not forgetting the wrong but doing the harder thing, facing it together and refusing to let it have the last word. Scripture makes peace so urgent that it tells the worshiper to leave the altar and go set things right first, as if a severed relationship interrupts even our worship.

topics.label: Mental Exhaustion and Burnout
topics.line: Exhaustion is not a character flaw to push through but a limit to be honored.
topics.framing: Exhaustion is not a character flaw to push through but a limit to be honored. Scripture made the limit into a command, building a Sabbath into the week and a rest into the very fabric of creation, and it does not praise the one who burns out but the one who learns to stop.

topics.label: Mentoring and Discipling
topics.line: Mentoring is not a program but a life lived close enough to be copied.
topics.framing: Mentoring is not a program but a life lived close enough to be copied. Scripture passes the faith down not mainly through lectures but through proximity, an older life walking beside a younger one, so that what is caught is character before it is competence.

topics.label: Miscarriage and Pregnancy Loss
topics.line: A miscarriage is the death of a child whom you loved before you ever held, and the grief is real even when others cannot see what was lost.
topics.framing: A miscarriage is the death of a child whom you loved before you ever held, and the grief is real even when others cannot see what was lost. Scripture does not treat the unborn as a possibility but as a person already known by God, knit together in secret, named before a single day had come.

topics.label: Money and Provision
topics.line: Scripture treats money as a matter of the heart, where the treasure is, there the heart will be also.
topics.framing: Scripture treats money as a matter of the heart, where the treasure is, there the heart will be also. It does not condemn the thing but warns that the love of it, not the having of it, is a root of every kind of evil.

topics.label: Moving and Relocation
topics.line: To move is to pull up roots, and the ache of it is real even when the move is good.
topics.framing: To move is to pull up roots, and the ache of it is real even when the move is good. Scripture is full of people sent to places they did not choose, and it gives the displaced a steadying word, that the God who calls you to go has already gone ahead, and no place is outside his presence.

topics.label: New Parenthood
topics.line: A child arrives and the floor of your life shifts under you.
topics.framing: A child arrives and the floor of your life shifts under you. Scripture calls children a heritage and a reward, and in the same breath it never pretends the gift is light, for the same God who gives the child also carries the parent through the long sleepless nights.

topics.label: Nostalgia and Longing for the Past
topics.line: Longing for the past is a kind of homesickness, and not all of it is a lie.
topics.framing: Longing for the past is a kind of homesickness, and not all of it is a lie. Scripture takes the ache seriously without letting it trap you, warning against gilding a past that was never as good as you remember, while pointing the homesick heart toward a home that is still ahead.

topics.label: Numbness and Feeling Nothing
topics.line: Numbness is not the same as peace.
topics.framing: Numbness is not the same as peace. It is often the heart's way of bracing against more pain than it can hold, and Scripture does not shame the one who has gone quiet inside but speaks of a heart of stone being given back its flesh.

topics.label: Obedience and Following God
topics.line: Obedience has fallen on hard times, mistaken for either grim duty or earning a place we already have.
topics.framing: Obedience has fallen on hard times, mistaken for either grim duty or earning a place we already have. Scripture frames it differently, as the natural shape of love and trust, the way a child follows a parent he believes is good. It is not the price of being loved but the proof that we believe we are.

topics.label: Opening Your Home
topics.line: Hospitality in Scripture is not entertaining, which performs for the admiration of guests, but welcome, which makes room for the stranger at real cost.
topics.framing: Hospitality in Scripture is not entertaining, which performs for the admiration of guests, but welcome, which makes room for the stranger at real cost. The word itself means love of the stranger, and the Bible ties it to the strange possibility that in welcoming the unknown guest you may be welcoming far more than you knew.

topics.label: Outrage Culture
topics.line: Outrage feels like conviction, and that is its danger.
topics.framing: Outrage feels like conviction, and that is its danger. It dresses itself in the clothes of justice while it trains the heart in contempt, and it spreads faster than any sober truth. Scripture is not impressed by our heat. It says plainly that the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God.

topics.label: Overeating and the Table
topics.line: Food is a good gift, and the table is one of Scripture's most honored places.
topics.framing: Food is a good gift, and the table is one of Scripture's most honored places. The struggle is not with eating but with the hunger underneath it, the reaching for the plate to fill what the plate was never able to fill.

topics.label: Overthinking
topics.line: Overthinking is the mind trying to control by rehearsal what it cannot control at all.
topics.framing: Overthinking is the mind trying to control by rehearsal what it cannot control at all. Scripture does not call you to think less but to think rightly, setting the racing mind on what is true and handing the unsolvable back to the only One who holds tomorrow.

topics.label: Parenting Adult Children
topics.line: There comes a day when the parent must stop steering and start blessing, when the open hand replaces the firm grip.
topics.framing: There comes a day when the parent must stop steering and start blessing, when the open hand replaces the firm grip. Scripture honors the long love of a parent while it also makes room for the child to leave, to cleave, to become a person before God in their own right.

topics.label: Parenting Struggles
topics.line: No one parents from a position of mastery.
topics.framing: No one parents from a position of mastery. Scripture hands the work to ordinary parents, tells them to teach as they walk and sit and lie down, and never pretends it will be clean or finished by Friday.

topics.label: Parenting Young Children
topics.line: The early years are not a delay before the real parenting begins.
topics.framing: The early years are not a delay before the real parenting begins. They are the parenting, the slow patient shaping of a small soul by ten thousand ordinary moments no one will applaud. Scripture frames children as a gift and a charge, given not to be owned but to be raised toward God and then released.

topics.label: Patience and Waiting
topics.line: Patience is not a passive temperament you either have or lack.
topics.framing: Patience is not a passive temperament you either have or lack. Scripture treats it as a fruit grown over time, the willingness to bear with people and circumstances that do not move on your schedule, and it names the patient man stronger than the warrior.

topics.label: Peace and Calm
topics.line: The peace Scripture offers is not mainly the absence of conflict but the presence of a wholeness, the Hebrew shalom, things set right with God, with others, and within.
topics.framing: The peace Scripture offers is not mainly the absence of conflict but the presence of a wholeness, the Hebrew shalom, things set right with God, with others, and within. It is a peace given rather than achieved, one that does not depend on the storm stopping and that Jesus said the world cannot give.

topics.label: People-Pleasing and the Fear of Man
topics.line: Scripture has an old, exact name for this: the fear of man, the dread of others' opinion that lays a snare for the feet.
phrases: cant handle anyone being upset with me
worried what everyone thinks of me
say yes so nobody gets upset
topics.framing: Scripture has an old, exact name for this: the fear of man, the dread of others' opinion that lays a snare for the feet. It is not the same as kindness; it is kindness hollowed out by fear, and the cure is not to care less for people but to fear God more, which strangely sets you free to love them.

topics.label: Perfectionism
topics.line: Perfectionism looks like high standards but often runs on fear, the dread of being found wanting, of resting only when the work is flawless and you with it.
topics.framing: Perfectionism looks like high standards but often runs on fear, the dread of being found wanting, of resting only when the work is flawless and you with it. Scripture does call us to be perfect as the Father is perfect, but the word means whole, mature, complete, not error-free, and it is grace, not anxiety, that gets us there.

topics.label: Persecution and Opposition
topics.line: Jesus never promised his followers the favor of the crowd.
topics.framing: Jesus never promised his followers the favor of the crowd. He promised the opposite, and then called it blessing, telling those who are reviled and shut out to rejoice rather than to recoil.

topics.label: Perseverance and Endurance
topics.line: Perseverance is not gritting your teeth alone.
topics.framing: Perseverance is not gritting your teeth alone. Scripture treats it as the long obedience that suffering itself produces, the muscle that grows under load, and it promises that the one who does not give up in the season of weariness will, in time, reap.

topics.label: Politics and Division
topics.line: The deepest line the Bible draws is not between left and right but between the kingdom of God and every kingdom that would claim your final loyalty.
topics.framing: The deepest line the Bible draws is not between left and right but between the kingdom of God and every kingdom that would claim your final loyalty. A faith captured by a political tribe has already traded its birthright. The danger is not that you hold convictions. It is that the tribe, not Christ, has become the thing you will not betray.

topics.label: Pornography and Its Grip
topics.line: If this has hold of you, hear first that you are not beyond reach and you are not alone in it.
topics.framing: If this has hold of you, hear first that you are not beyond reach and you are not alone in it. Scripture does not minimize the wound, but it speaks to it with grace before law, and the way out begins not with hating yourself harder but with bringing the secret into the light.

topics.label: Pride
topics.line: Pride is not loud confidence so much as the quiet conviction that the world should orbit you.
topics.framing: Pride is not loud confidence so much as the quiet conviction that the world should orbit you. Scripture names it the oldest sin and the root of the rest, and answers it not by crushing the self but by lifting the eyes off the self entirely.

topics.label: Procrastination and Laziness
topics.line: Scripture has a hard, almost comic honesty about the person who will not start, sending the sluggard to school under the ant and watching him roll on his bed like a door on its hinges.
topics.framing: Scripture has a hard, almost comic honesty about the person who will not start, sending the sluggard to school under the ant and watching him roll on his bed like a door on its hinges. It does not call the problem a personality; it calls it a choice, and it calls the choice costly.

topics.label: Purpose and Meaning
topics.line: The Bible does not hand you a private purpose to discover so much as a maker who already knows what you are for.
topics.framing: The Bible does not hand you a private purpose to discover so much as a maker who already knows what you are for. Meaning is not invented out of your own head. It is received, in being known by God and bent toward the good of others.

topics.label: Raising Teenagers
topics.line: Raising a teenager is the slow, deliberate work of handing over the controls before you are ready, so that the child becomes an adult who can stand on their own faith and not just yours.
phrases: on the phone all the time
topics.framing: Raising a teenager is the slow, deliberate work of handing over the controls before you are ready, so that the child becomes an adult who can stand on their own faith and not just yours. Scripture aims parents not at compliance but at the heart, and warns sharply against provoking the very rebellion you fear.

topics.label: Regret and the Past
topics.line: Regret is grief aimed backward, the ache of a road not taken or a wrong that cannot be undone.
topics.framing: Regret is grief aimed backward, the ache of a road not taken or a wrong that cannot be undone. Scripture does not pretend the past can be edited, but it draws a sharp line between the regret that leads to repentance and life and the regret that only circles the wound, and it promises a God who can redeem even the wasted years.

topics.label: Rest and Sabbath
topics.line: Rest is not the reward for finishing your work.
topics.framing: Rest is not the reward for finishing your work. It is a command, given by a God who rested when nothing forced him to, and a weekly declaration that the world holds together without you. To keep a Sabbath is to confess that you are not God, and to be glad of it.

topics.label: Restlessness
topics.line: Restlessness is not always a problem to be solved.
topics.framing: Restlessness is not always a problem to be solved. It is often the soul telling the truth, that it was made for more than it has found, and Scripture treats that ache not as a flaw to suppress but as a signpost pointing past every lesser rest.

topics.label: Retirement
topics.line: The work that defined your days ends, and the question underneath the gold watch is what your life is for now.
topics.framing: The work that defined your days ends, and the question underneath the gold watch is what your life is for now. Scripture has no category for a retreat into mere leisure, but it does offer something better, a final season aimed not at the self but at finishing well and handing on what you have gathered.

topics.label: Returning to God
topics.line: The whole of Scripture turns on one repeated mercy: that the way back is always open.
topics.framing: The whole of Scripture turns on one repeated mercy: that the way back is always open. Repentance is not crawling back to a reluctant God but turning toward a Father who has been watching the road. The shame that tells you it is too late, that you have used up your chances, is the one voice the gospel most flatly contradicts.

topics.label: Revenge and Getting Even
topics.line: The wish to get even feels like justice from the inside, but it almost never restores what was taken and almost always costs the one who carries it.
topics.framing: The wish to get even feels like justice from the inside, but it almost never restores what was taken and almost always costs the one who carries it. Scripture does not dismiss the wrong done to you, it takes it more seriously than you do, and then asks you to hand it to a Judge who will not get it wrong.

topics.label: Saving and Spending
topics.line: How you handle money is a window into the heart, and the question is not only how much you have but what owns you.
topics.framing: How you handle money is a window into the heart, and the question is not only how much you have but what owns you. Scripture honors the wisdom that gathers little by little and warns against both the hoarding that trusts in barns and the spending that chases a wind, calling you instead to the freedom of the open and steady hand.

topics.label: Saying No
topics.line: A no you mean is worth more than a yes you resent.
topics.framing: A no you mean is worth more than a yes you resent. Scripture does not praise the man who carries everything, but the one who knows his limits, keeps his word, and does not let his speech swell beyond what he can deliver. To say no clearly is to honor the yes you have already given.

topics.label: Self-Control and Discipline
topics.line: Self-control is not white-knuckled willpower but a fruit grown slowly by the Spirit, the steady governance of a life that has learned to want the right things.
topics.framing: Self-control is not white-knuckled willpower but a fruit grown slowly by the Spirit, the steady governance of a life that has learned to want the right things. Scripture compares the person without it to a city with its walls broken down, open to every raid.

topics.label: Self-Doubt
topics.line: Self-doubt asks the right question of the wrong judge.
topics.framing: Self-doubt asks the right question of the wrong judge. The issue was never whether you are enough on your own, you are not, and neither am I, but whose verdict you will finally trust, and Scripture moves your worth off your performance and onto the One who made and loves you.

topics.label: Self-Hatred
topics.line: Self-hatred is not humility, though it often disguises itself as such.
phrases: hate the person in the mirror
topics.framing: Self-hatred is not humility, though it often disguises itself as such. It is a verdict you have passed on a person God refused to throw away, and Scripture meets it not by flattering you but by telling you whose you are and what your maker paid to keep you.

topics.label: Self-Pity
topics.line: Self-pity is the grief that curdled, the sorrow that stopped looking for God and began collecting evidence against him.
topics.framing: Self-pity is the grief that curdled, the sorrow that stopped looking for God and began collecting evidence against him. It feels like honesty about a real wound, but it slowly trades the comfort it could have for the small bitter pleasure of being wronged.

topics.label: Self-Righteousness
topics.line: Self-righteousness is the sin that hides inside obedience, the quiet conviction that I have earned what others have not.
topics.framing: Self-righteousness is the sin that hides inside obedience, the quiet conviction that I have earned what others have not. It is the most religious of the sins and the hardest to see, because it wears the face of virtue. Scripture warns that the one who thinks he stands by his own goodness has missed the gospel entirely.

topics.label: Selfishness
topics.line: Selfishness is the gravity of the fallen heart, the slow pull that bends everything back toward the self.
topics.framing: Selfishness is the gravity of the fallen heart, the slow pull that bends everything back toward the self. It is not always loud. More often it is the quiet assumption that my comfort, my schedule, and my preferences are the center the world should circle. Scripture calls us out of that orbit and toward the good of others.

topics.label: Sensitivity and Feeling Too Much
topics.line: To feel things deeply is not a defect to be hardened out of you.
topics.framing: To feel things deeply is not a defect to be hardened out of you. Scripture honors the tender heart, the one moved to weep and to mercy, and it shows us a Savior who was not numb to the world but pierced by it, moved with compassion at the sight of the crowds.

topics.label: Serving in the Church
topics.line: You were given gifts that were never meant to stay yours alone.
topics.framing: You were given gifts that were never meant to stay yours alone. Scripture frames service not as the extra work of the eager few but as the ordinary shape of belonging to a body, where every part matters and no part carries the whole. The aim is not to do everything but to do your part, faithfully and without resentment.

topics.label: Serving Others
topics.line: In the kingdom Jesus describes, greatness runs in reverse, the first becoming last and the leader becoming the servant of all.
topics.framing: In the kingdom Jesus describes, greatness runs in reverse, the first becoming last and the leader becoming the servant of all. Service is not a lower task for those without a platform. It is the very shape of the life Christ lived and the form love takes when it has hands.

topics.label: Setting Boundaries
topics.line: A boundary is not a wall against love but a fence around a life, so that the love you give is given on purpose and not bled out by accident.
topics.framing: A boundary is not a wall against love but a fence around a life, so that the love you give is given on purpose and not bled out by accident. Scripture honors limits as part of the made order, and even Jesus withdrew from the crowds that wanted more than he had decided to give.

topics.label: Sexual Purity and Desire
topics.line: Scripture takes desire seriously precisely because it takes the body seriously, treating sex not as dirty but as so weighty it belongs inside covenant.
topics.framing: Scripture takes desire seriously precisely because it takes the body seriously, treating sex not as dirty but as so weighty it belongs inside covenant. Purity in the Bible is not the absence of desire but desire rightly ordered, aimed at the place it was made for.

topics.label: Shame
topics.line: Guilt says you did a bad thing.
topics.framing: Guilt says you did a bad thing. Shame says you are a bad thing. Scripture meets the shamed not with a verdict of disgust but with a covering, a God who makes garments for the exposed and lifts the head that cannot look up.

topics.label: Sibling Conflict
topics.line: No one knows your wounds like the people who grew up beside you, and no rift cuts quite like the one with a brother or sister.
topics.framing: No one knows your wounds like the people who grew up beside you, and no rift cuts quite like the one with a brother or sister. Scripture is strikingly honest about feuding siblings, and it holds out the hope that even these oldest fractures can be healed, sometimes after long years.

topics.label: Singleness
topics.line: Singleness is not a waiting room or a lesser state.
phrases: single the rest of my life
topics.framing: Singleness is not a waiting room or a lesser state. Scripture treats it as a full life with its own freedom and calling, and it never measures a person's worth by whether someone chose to marry them.

topics.label: Social Media and Attention
topics.line: Your attention is not a neutral thing you happen to spend.
topics.framing: Your attention is not a neutral thing you happen to spend. It is the soil your soul grows in, and these tools are built by careful people to capture it and sell it. Scripture says guard your heart, for from it flow the springs of life, and your heart is largely formed by whatever you keep looking at.

topics.label: Spiritual Growth
topics.line: Growth in the Christian life is not self-improvement with a religious coat of paint.
topics.framing: Growth in the Christian life is not self-improvement with a religious coat of paint. It is being slowly remade into the likeness of Christ, mostly through ordinary means and over long stretches of time, more like the seasons than the switch.

topics.label: Spiritual Pride
topics.line: Spiritual pride is the most dangerous sin precisely because it grows in the soil of real devotion.
topics.framing: Spiritual pride is the most dangerous sin precisely because it grows in the soil of real devotion. It takes the gifts of grace and turns them into a ledger of superiority, the very thing it congratulates itself on having escaped. It is the only sin that gets stronger the holier you become, hiding inside the virtues it corrupts.

topics.label: Spiritual Warfare
topics.line: The Bible tells you that you live on a contested ground, that there is a real enemy who is a liar and an accuser, and that the fight is fought not mainly in dramatic moments but in the daily work of standing firm.
topics.framing: The Bible tells you that you live on a contested ground, that there is a real enemy who is a liar and an accuser, and that the fight is fought not mainly in dramatic moments but in the daily work of standing firm. The aim is not fear of the dark but confidence in the One who has already won.

topics.label: Starting Over
topics.line: The God of Scripture is in the business of beginning again.
topics.framing: The God of Scripture is in the business of beginning again. He does not write people off at their lowest point but specializes in the second chapter, making new things out of ruined ones and people out of the wreckage they made.

topics.label: Status and Recognition
topics.line: The hunger to be recognized is not a modern invention, only a newly measured one, now counted in followers and likes.
topics.framing: The hunger to be recognized is not a modern invention, only a newly measured one, now counted in followers and likes. Scripture does not crush the desire to matter but reorders it, warning against doing good to be seen by others, and pointing the heart toward an audience of One who already sees in secret.

topics.label: Stealing and Taking
topics.line: Stealing is bigger than the empty pocket of the person robbed.
topics.framing: Stealing is bigger than the empty pocket of the person robbed. It is the choice to take what you have not earned and to make another bear the cost, and Scripture answers it not only with a stop but with a strange and hopeful turn toward giving.

topics.label: Stewardship
topics.line: Stewardship begins with a single fact, that nothing you hold is finally your own.
topics.framing: Stewardship begins with a single fact, that nothing you hold is finally your own. Time, money, gifts, the body, the earth itself are entrusted, not owned, and the question is never simply what you want to do with them but what the Owner would have you do.

topics.label: Stubbornness
topics.line: Stubbornness is the strength of conviction turned to stone.
topics.framing: Stubbornness is the strength of conviction turned to stone. There is a holy firmness that holds the line when everything pushes against it, and there is a hardness that simply refuses to bend because bending feels like losing. Scripture honors the first and warns relentlessly of the second, the stiff neck that will not turn even when God himself is the one calling.

topics.label: Submitting to Leaders
topics.line: Scripture asks Christians to honor and submit to their leaders, and the command makes many of us flinch, because we have seen authority abused and called holy.
topics.framing: Scripture asks Christians to honor and submit to their leaders, and the command makes many of us flinch, because we have seen authority abused and called holy. But the same Bible binds the leader far harder than the led, demanding shepherds who guard the flock rather than fleece it, who lead by example and not by force.

topics.label: Success and Failure
topics.line: Scripture refuses both the worship of success and the despair of failure.
topics.framing: Scripture refuses both the worship of success and the despair of failure. It measures a life not by the heights it reaches but by the faithfulness it keeps, and it tells the story of God working through the failed, the overlooked, and the ones who had to start again. Your worst chapter is not your verdict.

topics.label: Sudden and Traumatic Loss
topics.line: When death comes without warning, there is no time to brace, no chance to say goodbye, only the shock of a world that was whole this morning and shattered by night.
topics.framing: When death comes without warning, there is no time to brace, no chance to say goodbye, only the shock of a world that was whole this morning and shattered by night. Scripture does not soften the violence of such loss, but it anchors the reeling heart to a God who is a refuge and a present help precisely in the trouble that arrives without notice.

topics.label: Suicidal Thoughts
topics.line: If you are thinking of ending your life, your pain is real and it deserves to be taken seriously, but the thought it is telling you, that there is no way through, is lying to you.
topics.framing: If you are thinking of ending your life, your pain is real and it deserves to be taken seriously, but the thought it is telling you, that there is no way through, is lying to you. You are not a burden, you are not beyond help, and the God who made you has not let go of you, even when you have lost your grip on him.

topics.label: Surrender and Letting Go
topics.line: Surrender is the word the modern ear most resists, because it sounds like defeat.
topics.framing: Surrender is the word the modern ear most resists, because it sounds like defeat. In Scripture it is the opposite, the opening of a clenched fist that has been tired for years, the release of a control we never actually had. To surrender to God is not to lose the self but to stop carrying what was never ours to carry.
